summary_for_children: Al-Ma'un means Small Kindnesses. It warns against pushing away orphans, not feeding the poor, praying to show off and refusing small help.
environment_concept: A small morning street: a home with an open door and a bench (107:2), a table with bread and water (107:3) and a shelf of small things to lend, like a bucket and a pot (107:7). No people are shown.
architecture_and_scenery: Low homes, an open doorway with a bench, a table, a lending shelf, a well.

areas.name: The Open Door
areas.description: A home with its door open and a bench outside: the opposite of driving the orphan away.

areas.name: The Bread Table
areas.description: A table set with bread and water, ready to share.

areas.name: Lending Shelf
areas.description: A shelf of small things to lend: a bucket, a pot, a rope.

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Little Acts of Kindness
story_library.children_narration: Sometimes a small helpful action can make a big difference. Surah Al-Ma'un reminds us to care for orphans and people in need and not to turn worship into something done only to impress others. Sincere kindness matters.

world_idea.title: The Village of Helping Hands
world_idea.description: Help fictional neighbors by sharing useful household items, preparing supplies, and practicing thoughtful community care.
